title: North Star: can you see what it's thinking?
blurb: The whole course as one night walk across a torn-paper map of 14 Saturdays, while a sealed mind egg slowly turns to glass. Ends with a tappable map of every week.

title: Every shape has a story
blurb: A night-shift librarian sorts 24 paper tiles into a (2, 3, 4) tensor, flattens it with einops, unrolls a VHS batch, stretches stamps by broadcasting, matchmakes an einsum, and fires a batch of rays at a wall. Then drive the tiles and the torch yourself.

title: The little window that learned to see
blurb: A red paper View-Master window hunts for a cat in an 8x8 Game Boy picture: real multiply-and-sum at every click, one rubber stamp for weight sharing, max-pool keeps the loudest voice, receptive fields grow, a paper plane takes the ResNet express lane x + f(x), and a volume knob does BatchNorm. Ends with a paintable grid and editable kernel.

title: Which way is down, and how big a step?
blurb: A paper hiker on a real loss surface: SGD zig-zags, learning rates too small and too big, momentum as a heavy marble, Adam's two running averages. Then race all three yourself.

title: Adam, line by line
blurb: Deep dive for [0.3]: why √v gives every parameter its own ruler (loss ×100, Adam's path doesn't budge), noisy minibatches, bias correction at step 1 with real numbers (3.16·lr raw, 31.6·lr half-fixed, exactly lr fixed) with a predict-then-watch pause, epsilon's job, AdamW vs L2-in-the-gradient (34× unequal squeeze), the per-coordinate limit, and your own torch-style step().

title: Who gets the blame?
blurb: A paper factory on the night shift: a plane carries 1.5 forward through ×w, +b, tanh and a squared error until the bell rings. Then rewind the Walkman and watch the blame relay backwards, station by station, summing where the line splits. Then drive x, w, b and the target yourself and check backprop against wiggling.

title: Building autograd from scratch
blurb: Deep dive for [0.4]: every tensor carries a Recipe, BACK_FUNCS gives local slopes, fan-out grads add with +=, sorted_computational_graph sets the order, unbroadcast sums copied axes, matmul backward by shapes, then your own backprop loop. Includes a predict-then-watch pause.

title: The shared notebook
blurb: A paper school corridor where every token is a pupil with a notebook (the residual stream). Real softmax attention over q·k scores, a causal mask, an MLP card catalogue, LayerNorm as a Walkman volume wheel, and next-word lanterns. Then aim the query yourself.

title: Choose a word, open the hood
blurb: The mind egg picks its next word: logits as lanterns on poles, a temperature dial, top-k snipping and a top-p ribbon, a KV-cache recipe box, then a plumber opens the pipes, photographs every activation and closes one head's tap. Then drive T, k, p and the taps yourself.

title: Haven't I seen this before?
blurb: A paper VHS tape of random words plays twice. A previous-token clerk stamps each card, an induction clerk finds the stamp and copies the next word; live softmax attention, per-token loss, a probe ruler, a steering arrow and SAE lanterns. Coda: record a tape, sharpen QK, slide a steering coefficient.

title: Which part matters?
blurb: Two paper dollhouses tell the IOI story, one with names swapped. A repair person patches one room (head) at a time and a logit-difference seesaw swings back, filling a real recovery heatmap; then five lodgers share two rooms (superposition) and a backup head hides importance. Coda: tap rooms to patch, slide feature density.

title: What is this square worth?
blurb: A paper robot on a cliff-walk board game: Bellman ripples, live Q-learning TD updates, SARSA the cautious cousin, a DQN replay shoebox with a frozen target, and a dancer learning by applause (policy gradient).

title: How far can I trust this step?
blurb: A climber on a foggy ridge learns advantage and the PPO clip (live ratio, flat past 1+ε), then the mind egg writes postcards for a learned judge: reward model from preferences, !!!!!! reward hacking, and the KL leash to a frozen reference.

title: Measure it, then contain it
blurb: A paper detective pins a threat model with red string, turns it into a spec, grows a 300-question dataset (a grader tears up weak items), then runs an Inspect-style eval with live accuracy and 95% intervals. Tools reveal hidden capability; a THIS IS A TEST sign raises eval awareness. Then AI control: an untrusted coder, a trusted monitor and a 2% audit budget, with safety simulated by Monte-Carlo and a Win98 results sheet. Coda: slide audit, defer and monitor quality; live safety vs usefulness frontier.

title: From hunch to experiment
blurb: A capstone student turns a hunch (narrow fine-tuning makes models broadly misaligned) into a falsifiable index card, hatches a LoRA model organism (live parameter counts), runs matched controls scored by an autorater with 95% intervals, sees a shutdown-resistance style one-variable ablation, scales a pilot until the bars separate, and steers along a persona vector. Then the first exciting result turns out to be a bug. Coda: slide n and true rates; live Wald and Wilson intervals plus simulated power.

title: Which step mattered?
blurb: Snip a chain of thought and let the model rewrite it 40 times: one sentence moves the answer (real KL from real counts). Then masks on an Assistant axis, a conversation that drifts, and activation capping that fences it back in. Drive the drift and the cap yourself.

title: Show your work
blurb: Presentation day in a paper school hall: one chart with real 95% error bars, a limits slide on an overhead transparency, an investigator agent and a realism filter for next time, a README to reproduce it, and a warm finale with every motif from the course. Then order your own five-minute talk against a live timer.
